title: AI consulting for marketing agencies | Creosote Labs
meta_description: Creosote Labs assesses where AI tools fit in a marketing agency's briefs, reporting, and client communication, then sets them up and trains staff.
intro: Marketing agencies often run client work across a project tool such as Asana, ClickUp, or Monday.com, with proposals and creative briefs in Google Docs, ad accounts in Google Ads and Meta Ads Manager, and monthly reporting pulled from Google Analytics into slide decks. Much of the writing an agency produces each week, including briefs, campaign summaries, and status updates, follows a repeatable format. AI consulting applies to that repeatable writing and to the reporting that sits behind it.

Creosote Labs starts with a one-day operations review of how the agency takes on a client, runs a campaign, and reports on it. The review produces a written assessment of where an AI tool the agency already has, such as Google Gemini, Microsoft 365 Copilot, or Claude, can draft first versions of briefs and reports from the agency's own templates. Each recommendation comes with a quote, and staff are trained on their own accounts and documents.
projects: A monthly client report drafted from Google Analytics and ad platform exports using the agency's report template.
A creative brief generator that turns a kickoff call transcript into a brief in the agency's format.
A proposal first draft assembled from the agency's past scopes of work and the prospect's intake notes.
A weekly client status email drafted from completed tasks in Asana or ClickUp.
A review of which AI tools the agency already pays for and how each should be set up for account teams.

faqs.q: Does the review cover client data and ad accounts?
faqs.a: Yes. The review looks at how briefs, reports, and campaigns move through the agency, including the data pulled from ad platforms and analytics. Client data stays in the agency's own accounts; we set up tools the agency already licenses rather than moving data elsewhere.

faqs.q: What does the operations review cost and what does the agency receive?
faqs.a: The one-day review is $3,000. It produces a written assessment and a quote for each recommendation, and implementation is quoted from that document.
Team training is $1,000 per person. It is delivered on the agency's own tools and documents and includes a written guide for the team.
